title: Weather fronts and clouds
examples: What is the difference between a warm and cold front?
How does air pressure change before a storm?
Can you name a cloud that forms high up?

explain.say: Today we are learning about weather fronts and clouds.

items: Weather Fronts: Boundaries of air masses
Air Pressure: Changes in atmospheric weight

explain.say: A warm front happens when warm air rises over cold air.

draw.text: Warm Front: Warm air over cold

explain.say: A cold front happens when cooler, denser air moves in quickly.

items: Cold air rapidly pushes warm air
This lifting causes fast vertical cloud development

draw.text: Cold Front: Cold air pushes warm

explain.say: One common cloud type is cirrus clouds, which are high and wispy.
Another important cloud is cumulus, which are puffy and look like cotton balls.
Air pressure is the weight of the air above a certain spot.

draw.text: Air Pressure: Weight of air above

faq.q: Do warm fronts always mean rain?
faq.a: Warm fronts often bring steady, widespread rain or drizzle. This is because the gentle lifting of air causes condensation over a wide area.
asks: Will I get wet near a warm front?
What kind of precipitation do warm fronts cause?

faq.a: Cumulonimbus clouds are associated with severe weather, including heavy rain, thunder, and lightning. They are the largest and tallest type of cloud.
asks: Do these clouds mean a storm is coming?

faq.q: How can I tell if the air pressure is changing?
faq.a: You can often tell by looking at the sky. Falling pressure usually means a storm is approaching, while rising pressure suggests stable, clear weather.
asks: What does falling pressure mean for the weather?
How does air pressure affect the sky?

faq.q: What is the difference between cirrus and stratus clouds?
faq.a: Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy, found very high up. Stratus clouds are more like a uniform, grey sheet covering the whole sky.
asks: What does a grey sheet cloud look like?

faq.q: If the air pressure is low, what weather should I expect?
faq.a: Low air pressure is typically associated with rising air masses. This rising air cools and condenses, leading to cloud formation and potentially stormy weather.
asks: Is low pressure always bad weather?

facts: Warm fronts involve the gradual lifting of air, often causing steady precipitation.
Cold fronts involve rapid air movement, typically leading to sharp changes in weather.
Cirrus clouds are composed of ice crystals and are found at very high altitudes.
High air pressure usually indicates sinking air, which suppresses cloud formation.

quiz.say: When cool air rapidly pushes under warm air, what type of front is usually present?
quiz.why: Cold fronts involve rapid, forceful movement of air, which causes dramatic weather changes.

wrong.0: Pressure describes the air weight, not the boundary itself.
wrong.2: Warm fronts are slow and gradual, not rapid pushes.
wrong.3: This is not a standard term for a weather boundary.

quiz.say: If the sky is covered by a uniform, grey sheet cloud, which cloud type might this be?
quiz.why: Stratus clouds are known for covering the sky in a flat, uniform layer.

wrong.1: Cirrus clouds are thin and wispy, not a solid sheet.
wrong.2: Cumulus clouds are puffy and distinct, not uniform.
wrong.3: While similar, stratus is the general term for the sheet appearance.

quiz.say: If the air pressure is very high, what weather condition is most likely?
quiz.why: High pressure means air is sinking, which warms and dries the air, preventing cloud formation.

wrong.0: Thunderstorms usually form under low pressure conditions.
wrong.1: Steady rain is more often linked to the lifting mechanism of a warm front.
wrong.2: Overcast skies can happen at any pressure, but high pressure suggests stability.
